_comment: Shared contract between two implementations of the same algorithm: re-projecting
stored polygons through the geometric edits rgb_editor.js applied to the image
under them. The client half is frontend/imaging/photos/editReplay.js and the
They existed independently and had drifted: the server implemented flip-h, flip-v
and crop and NOT rotate-cw or rotate-arbitrary, so a rotated photograph read back
untransformed polygons -- the segmentation quietly detached from the anatomy. This
file is what stops that happening again: both test suites read it, and a change to
either implementation that is not matched in the other fails on both sides.
Expected values are rounded to 3 decimals, which is what both implementations do.
Add a case here before fixing a bug in either one.

cases.name: no operations leaves the polygon alone
flip-h mirrors x about the image width
flip-v mirrors y about the image height
a crop wholly containing the polygon is a translation
a crop cutting the polygon clips it and closes along the cut
a crop that excludes the polygon entirely drops it
rotate-cw is a quarter turn about the image, not about the origin
rotate-arbitrary by zero degrees only re-origins into the bounding box
rotate-arbitrary by 90 degrees, with the bounding box the editor computes
operations compose in order: flip then crop
cases._note: the mirror reverses which vertex is which; the ring is the same, walked from the other corner

cases.name: the same two operations in the other order give a different answer
an unknown operation is the identity, so an image stays openable
